name: suzukiiichiro.github.io
summary: The published blog behind the N-Queens repository, written in Japanese. Forty posts mention Codon, walking through the bit-level solver implementations and their timings. The largest body of Codon writing found in the index, and the companion to the code entry rather than a separate project.
why_codon: The posts document Codon implementations of the N-Queens solvers alongside the other languages the author compares.

name: Python-practice
summary: A large notebook collection covering Python techniques, two of whose notebooks are about Codon: one introducing it as a Python compiler, and one on real multithreading in Python through it. Teaching material aimed at working Python programmers rather than compiler people.
why_codon: One notebook presents Codon as a Python compiler; the other presents it as the route to real multithreading in Python, which is a claim about the GIL rather than about compilation speed.
note: The multithreading framing is the only place in the index where Codon is presented primarily as an escape from the GIL rather than as an optimizing compiler.

name: toolmaker-berlin/init
summary: A personal notes repository whose Codon page, written in German and dated March 2024, records the commands worth remembering: running and building the same Fibonacci program as .codon and as .py, timed against PyPy, with a decorator that measures elapsed milliseconds. A working note rather than an article.
why_codon: The note times the same program under Codon run, Codon build and PyPy, so the comparison against the alternative Python accelerator is the point.
note: Shows a user treating .codon and .py as interchangeable inputs, running both forms of the same program in adjacent lines. A small piece of evidence for why the extension search misses so much -- see docs/gaps.md.

name: AriESQ/stars
summary: An archive of one user's starred repositories, storing each project's README alongside a manifest. Codon's README is one of them, so the entry records that Codon was starred and mirrored rather than used.
why_codon: No claim of its own; Codon's own README is archived among many others.
note: The weakest entry in the index. Kept because the mention lane is a real channel, but it carries no information about Codon beyond the fact of a star.

name: cainiaoprogram.github.io
summary: A published Chinese-language programming blog carrying a post on Codon, reproducing its usage and the run-release invocation.
why_codon: No claim beyond introducing the compiler and its invocation to a general programming audience.
note: With the Japanese N-Queens blog and the German notes, the mention lane spans four languages. Codon's documentation reaches beyond English writing even where its code does not.
